final_recommendation: The room converged on a negotiated settlement: FINMA commits to 30% recovery in writing by Friday with independent asset verification and binding equity-depletion-first precedent language; counsel stands down filing permanently. Market repositioning contingent on FINMA's enforcement credibility on future issuers.
minority_objections: Institutional investor expressed residual uncertainty about whether FINMA would actually enforce equity-first on the next issuer, requiring proof of enforcement before full AT1 repositioning
Insurance observer flagged that D&O defense costs would restart if counsel re-dockets Monday due to weak enforcement signals
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel initially demanded 40% recovery and threatened immediate NY filing; FINMA countered that settlement authority required board approval and multi-party process
Counsel insisted on binding precedent language (equity-depletion-first as legal precondition) while FINMA initially offered only procedural framework without hard recovery number
Market participants demanded clarity on whether equity-first applied to all future issuers or was CS-specific; FINMA resisted committing beyond the immediate case until final rounds
key_concessions: FINMA moved from 15% exploratory floor to 25% binding floor to final 30% with asset-recovery upside and independent verification
Bondholder counsel dropped from 40% demand to accepting 30% with verification and binding precedent language
FINMA committed to explicit equity-depletion-first language as legal precondition for all future viability events, not just CS-specific clarification
Counsel agreed to stand down filing permanently (not just pause) if 30% + precedent language delivered by Friday
red_lines: Counsel: 30% minimum recovery with independent asset verification and binding equity-first precedent language—anything less triggers Monday filing
FINMA: settlement framework must stay within regulatory authority (no unilateral commitments exceeding board approval scope)
Market participants: equity-depletion-first must apply as binding rule to all future issuers, not case-specific interpretation
Bondholder group: no settlement validates hierarchy inversion without explicit precedent correction
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Enforcement credibility gap: institutional investor flagged that market repositioning depends on seeing FINMA enforce equity-first on the *next* issuer, not just writing it down—room did not develop contingency if FINMA fails that test

Coverage dispute tail: insurance observer noted D&O insurers will fight 'known loss' exclusions dating to March 19 ordinance, potentially reducing net recovery by 30-40%, but room did not model impact on final settlement economics

Cross-border litigation complexity: counsel filed in NY and Geneva naming board/advisers, but room did not explore jurisdictional conflicts or sovereign immunity defenses that could fragment the claims tail

Reputational damage to Swiss regulatory framework: no participant developed how this settlement (or litigation) affects Switzerland's standing as financial center or future crisis-resolution credibility
downstream_risk_variables: AT1 issuance freeze duration: market confidence at 28-31 throughout; unclear whether 30% settlement + precedent letter actually unfreezes issuance or just narrows spreads
D&O/E&O claims accumulation: 40-60M defense costs for directors, 15-25M for advisers, plus FINMA E&O exposure—settlement stops the burn but does not reverse costs already incurred

Precedent enforcement test: institutional investor explicitly stated repositioning contingent on FINMA enforcing equity-first on next issuer; if that fails, settlement credibility collapses and litigation restarts
Asset recovery materialization risk: 30% floor with upside to 32-35% depends on CS residual asset pool; if recovery falls short, bondholder group may challenge settlement adequacy
Regulatory legitimacy erosion: FINMA's emergency ordinance procedural bypass remains contested; settlement does not resolve underlying constitutional/parliamentary authority questions
uncertainty_notes: Settlement hinges on FINMA delivering binding precedent language by Friday and institutional investors believing FINMA will enforce equity-first on future issuers. If either fails, counsel re-dockets Monday and litigation tail extends 4-6 years. Asset recovery upside (30% → 35%) depends on CS residual pool materialization, which remains unverified. D&O/E&O defense costs already incurred (est. 40-60M) are sunk regardless of settlement. Market repositioning (AT1 confidence at 28-31) may lag settlement by months if enforcement credibility remains unproven.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the central forcing mechanism throughout: counsel threatened NY filing in R1, filed naming board/KPMG in R6, and only stood down permanently in R8 after 30% + precedent language secured. Every major concession (25% floor, 30% final, binding precedent) was extracted under explicit filing threat.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's emergency ordinance procedural bypass (no Parliament) and viability-event interpretation were contested in R1-R3, but the room pivoted to settlement mechanics rather than building a sustained constitutional challenge. Counsel focused on hierarchy inversion and contract terms, not ordinance legitimacy itself.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (AT1 wiped, equity preserved) was the foundational grievance driving every round: bondholder group in R1 called it 'indefensible,' counsel in R3-R4 anchored all demands on correcting the precedent, and FINMA's equity-depletion-first commitment in R8 was the settlement's core term. This was decision-driving throughout.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing (300bps wider, issuance frozen 18 months) was raised by credit analyst in R1-R2 and institutional investor in R5-R8, but the room treated it as context for settlement urgency rather than modeling contagion mechanics or developing market-stabilization measures. Medium weight, not dominant.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: D&O defense costs (40-60M), E&O exposure, and 4-6 year litigation duration were raised by insurance observer in R1-R4 and used as settlement leverage, but the room did not structure the tail's breadth (multi-party, cross-border), severity distribution, or reinsurance accumulation as a formal risk model. Discussed but not deeply developed.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O exposure was explicitly raised by insurance observer in R1-R4 and R6-R8 as settlement leverage (40-60M defense costs, coverage disputes on 'known loss' exclusions), and counsel's decision to name board/advisers in R6 was framed as activating insurer exposure. Concrete and recurring, but not the room's primary driver—used tactically rather than as a standalone risk thread.
